html:
Augusto Roa Bastos was a Paraguayan novelist, the most famous writer of his country. His novel I, the Supreme, of 1974, is one of the great Latin American novels about dictatorship.

He served in the Chaco War as a teenager and wrote about it in Son of Man (1960). He went into exile in Argentina in 1947 after a civil war and later lived in France, returning to Paraguay only after the fall of Stroessner.

I, the Supreme imagines the mind of the dictator Francia through his notes and dictations, mixing Spanish and Guarani ways of telling. It is read as a book about all dictators. In 1989 he won the Cervantes Prize, the highest honour for writing in Spanish, and his work stands with that of García Márquez.
